situation: He completed a PhD in physics and was working within academia.
choice: He decided to leave academia because he felt he would never be a very good physicist.
outcome: He is now outside of academia and reflects on his studies positively.
main_reason: He believed he would never be a very good physicist despite loving teaching.
advice: Talk with physicists at average, local universities to get a realistic view of the job.
quote: I left academia after my PhD because I knew I would never be a very good physicist (though I loved to teach).
author: WoJ

situation: After two years of temporary academic positions, the author decided to leave academia.
choice: They chose to move into a cybersecurity career instead of staying in research.
outcome: They now work in cybersecurity, using communication skills, and continue math research as a hobby without academic pressures.
main_reason: Better salary and flexibility for independent research.
advice: Industry jobs can fund research and provide time freedom; staying in academia isn’t the only path to continue math.
quote: I left academia after two years of temporary positions, eventually migrating to a career in cybersecurity.
author: Jeremy Dover

situation: The author completed a 5.5‑year PhD in a theoretical field with three publications and then spent four more years in academia as a postdoc.
choice: They decided to leave academia and take a job in industry.
outcome: They are now working in industry, continue to publish research, and are very happy with the job.
main_reason: Postdoc jobs have low pay, poor work‑life balance, and limited entry barriers, making industry more attractive.
quote: After that I went to industry, I continue to do and to publish research and I'm very happy with my current job.
author: qbit-

situation: The author was in a top psychology PhD program during the second year.
choice: They quit the program halfway through the second year due to theoretical disagreements with professors.
outcome: They faced identity crisis, family reactions, and difficulty finding a job, eventually securing research coordinator positions after adjusting their resume and interviewing for entry‑level roles.
main_reason: Theoretical disagreements with professors and lack of fit with the program.
advice: Use a community career center to create a concise resume, withdraw fully from the program, research the new field, and be prepared to explain the departure honestly.
quote: I was still on my school’s website as a doctoral student and I was formally on a leave of absence, which was discordant with the “withdrew in good standing” statement on my resume. This created suspicion that I was just on a break from my program and probably contributed to being turned down.
author: Yolanda

situation: The author left a PhD program and entered industry work in the US.
choice: Quit the PhD to pursue a software engineering job.
outcome: Has been working as a software engineer at a big‑tech company for about 2.5 years.
main_reason: Believed a PhD was unnecessary for industry and wanted relevant technical experience.
advice: A PhD is not required for tech jobs; focus on experience and a master’s degree is sufficient.
quote: It’s been about 2 and a half years that I started working in industry in the US, after I quit my PhD and got a Master's degree (though I had another Master's before joining the PhD program).
author: Mithridates the Great

situation: She was an academic researcher feeling pressure to become a PI and worried about external validation.
choice: She left academia and became a clinician.
outcome: She now works as a clinician, does occasional research, enjoys broader conversations, and no longer tracks citations.
main_reason: She did not relish leading a research group and wanted to avoid feeling like a failure.
advice: Make like Elsa and let it go, releasing the need for external validation.
quote: I still lurk on Academia SO because I like to be reminded that my decision was right :)
author: Ottie

situation: The author turned down a PhD offer from their undergraduate advisor and left the PhD program, now taking a gap year.
choice: They decided to quit the PhD program.
outcome: They are currently on a gap year and have had mixed reactions from interviewers.
main_reason: Feeling dissatisfied with the program, advisor, and personal life balance.
quote: I've turned down a PhD offer from my undergraduate advisor this year and currently I'm taking a gap year.
author: user10517213

situation: He was a PhD student who was publicly insulted and harassed by a senior professor.
choice: He decided to leave academia.
outcome: He left academia and later reflects on the decision.
main_reason: The professor's harassment and the medieval academic culture.
advice: If you choose to fight, make sure you enjoy it because it will be very tough.
quote: I left academia mostly for this.
author: WoJ

situation: They taught biology students during their PhD in physics and later left academia after completing the degree.
choice: They decided to leave academia and pursue a job in industry.
outcome: Twenty‑five years later they work in industry and use their physics knowledge to help their children with math and physics.
main_reason: They felt academic teaching was disconnected from real‑world needs and wanted a more practical career.
advice: Simplify teaching to what learners need and focus on practical relevance.
quote: I left academia after my PhD and went into industry. It is now 25 years and I am faced with math and physics again when helping my children.
author: WoJ

situation: they were an unhappy lecturer in biostatistics after completing their PhD, feeling restless and dissatisfied with academic pressures.
choice: they quit their lectureship, moved countries, took a data‑science job, then left that job to become self‑employed and take a part‑time academic role.
outcome: they now work as a self‑employed freelancer combining academic research with entrepreneurship, feeling independent and satisfied with their work.
main_reason: they were unhappy with the academic environment and wanted more freedom and ownership of their research.
advice: they suggest persisting through early setbacks, not burning bridges, and being open to returning to academia later if needed.
quote: Leaving academia was the best thing I ever did, but be prepared for a shock to the system as you enter the "real world".
author: SoB

situation: they were an academic researcher considering moving to industry
choice: they decided to leave academia for an industrial research position
outcome: they say everything worked out well and they continue to write papers
main_reason: they wanted a change despite fear of leaving academia
advice: they advise not being afraid of change and staying involved in conferences
quote: everything worked out well, and I even get to writ
author: joe the publisher

situation: They left academia and had years of notes stored in folders and boxes.
choice: They decided the notes were pointless clutter and dumped them in the recycling.
outcome: They never looked at the notes again and now rely on books or online sources for information.
main_reason: The notes were seen as unnecessary clutter.
advice: Consider discarding old academic materials that no longer serve a purpose.
quote: I never looked at any of those notes again. Eventually, I just decided that they were pointless clutter and dumped them in the recycling.
author: Simon B

situation: they were a PhD student experiencing ups and downs and felt unable to continue
choice: they decided to quit their PhD program
outcome: they left the program and later received another opportunity a few years afterward
main_reason: they felt the situation was untenable and chose to quit
advice: they suggest talking to supervisors or department staff before quitting, as it can be a turning point
quote: Full disclosure: I quit my PhD. The first my supervisor heard of it was the day I quit. Luckily, someone else gave me another chance a few years later.
author: Dave Clarke

situation: They have finished five years of a PhD with five top‑tier publications that are unrelated, making a thesis impossible and losing their scholarship.
choice: They decided to complete the PhD by submitting two recent papers and obtaining the advisor’s permission.
outcome: If the two papers are published, they will be allowed to submit a thesis and receive a project assistantship salary while finishing.
main_reason: They care about earning the PhD and want to avoid leaving without it, and the advisor agreed to support the plan.
advice: Complete the PhD without antagonizing the advisor and wait for the two papers to be published.
quote: I have decided to complete my PhD without antagonizing my advisor.
author: user2808118

situation: They resigned and their last day fell on a public holiday, and the new employer wanted to move the end date earlier.
choice: They refused to change the end date, stating it would become a termination/dismissal.
outcome: The employer eventually paid them for the holiday, albeit grudgingly.
main_reason: To avoid being treated as a termination and facing an unfair dismissal claim.
advice: Check contract terms and push back on last‑day changes that affect pay or rights.
quote: I firmly said if they took such action, it would no longer be resignation and would instead be termination/dismissal, which would be met with an unfair dismissal claim (as this was in Australia).
author: fabspro

situation: They were working under a manager who wanted them gone and were eventually fired, and later they quit another job because of a senior colleague’s dislike.
choice: They decided to quit the job after the senior person’s behavior and the manager’s hostility.
outcome: They left the company; their boss acknowledged the senior’s dislike and tried to lure them to stay, which upset them but also made them smile.
main_reason: A senior colleague’s dislike and a hostile manager made the work environment untenable.
advice: Start a job search immediately, improve marketable skills, stay upbeat, volunteer for extra work, and align discussions with manager’s goals without appearing as a complainer.
quote: He also said something like "you've done such a great (and visible) job on the XXX project over the past 9 months that every time Steve bad-mouths you, he looks like an idiot. If you leave that stops".
author: Flydog57

situation: they were working as a developer and considering leaving their job
choice: they decided to resign from their position
outcome: they resigned a few months ago and completed a transition plan
main_reason: they wanted a new job and to finish their current project before leaving
advice: they recommend having a new job lined up and creating a detailed transition plan before resigning
quote: I resigned from a job a few months ago.
author: Matthew Gaiser

situation: they worked in IT for a bank in the City of London before 2007
choice: they quit their job to play poker professionally
outcome: they struggled to find employment afterward and only secured a new job in early 2011 after extensive checks
main_reason: they wanted to pursue a living playing poker
advice: hide the poker experience on a résumé if possible
quote: Eventually early in 2011 I found a group who was willing to take a chance on me.
author: TheMathemagician

situation: they were hired at a low rate and were promised a raise after passing probation
choice: they quit their job to work elsewhere after the promised raise was not delivered
outcome: they left the company and secured a higher‑pay position elsewhere
main_reason: the employer failed to honor the promised raise
advice: always get important promises in writing and don’t rely on a verbal agreement
quote: The sad truth is that if it's not in the contract, consider it a lie.
author: ptr

situation: they resigned their seventh job at Accenture after the company refused remote work
choice: they quit the job
outcome: they saw a psychiatrist and felt everything fell into place
main_reason: the employer would not allow them to work from home
advice: seek employers that explicitly offer remote work and ask about policies during interviews
author: Joe Strazzere

situation: they resigned from a job and their last day fell on a holiday
choice: they submitted a resignation with the holiday as the final date
outcome: the HR department paid them for the holiday days
main_reason: they wanted to leave the job
advice: do not accept a resignation date that falls on a holiday and ensure the employer pays up to the actual last working day
quote: As it happens this is exactly what happened when I resigned from a job once. They didn't notice at the time I submitted my resignation that my last day was a holiday and their HR insisted they pay me for it.
author: HLGEM

situation: they were employed at a company that did not meet their expectations
choice: they resigned from the job
outcome: they worked through the notice period but the company refused to give a proper reference
main_reason: the company failed to meet their expectations
advice: focus on what they learned during the stay, as the experience is better than starting with nothing
quote: The company did not meet my expectations so I resigned.
author: Jonast92

situation: they resigned from a company they had fun at and made many friends
choice: they decided to leave the company despite feeling it didn’t feel right
outcome: they now have a job that fits them better, feel better, and the previous company is running fine
main_reason: they wanted a role that better fits their preferences
advice: stay professional, don’t burn bridges, ask for referrals, thank the boss for the opportunity
quote: But now I have a job that fits me better, I feel better and my previous company is running just fine.
author: Kevin

situation: they were working at a job with no other position lined up
choice: they decided to quit their first job
outcome: their former employer continued operating without them
main_reason: they wanted to leave the job
advice: be helpful when leaving, don’t feel guilty, and you have no obligation to inform them in advance
quote: FWIW, when I quit my first job, I thought I was critical to their success and that they would have a hard time without me. Somehow, they survived.
author: Kristopher Johnson

situation: they were a software developer at a large corporate and felt the need for a change
choice: they quit their job without another one lined up
outcome: they spent four months traveling in South‑East Asia, are up‑skilling in web and mobile development, and are doing freelance work and a startup project
main_reason: they wanted flexibility to travel, learn new skills, and pursue personal projects
advice: they suggest reducing hours or finding part‑time work before quitting, networking, building an online profile, and confirming if a Silicon Valley job is truly desired
quote: Since then, I've spent 4 months travelling in South-East Asia. Now, I'm up-skilling in web and mobile development so I can either freelance or get part-time work in a smaller company.
author: Will J Thomas

situation: Their wife faced a complex legal case that threatened her business, requiring extensive support.
choice: They quit their software architect job to help manage the legal battle and assist with the business.
outcome: The legal case was resolved successfully after several years, and they are now ready to return to software work.
main_reason: To support their overwhelmed wife and handle the legal and business challenges.
advice: They can highlight improved written communication and ability to simplify complex issues under pressure on their CV.
quote: The legal battle had to be fought through a number of courts, taking several years before it concluded (successfully thankfully).
author: abc123

situation: They worked five years at a well‑known institution with high workloads, sexism, and a blame culture.
choice: They decided to quit their job.
outcome: They are preparing for a final meeting with their boss and worry about receiving a recommendation and being blamed for a project hand‑off.
main_reason: Toxic combination of overwork, sexism, and lack of support for women.

quote: My boss and I are having a final meeting.
author: angela

situation: They were a new contractor in the US working through multiple staffing agencies and were paid a very low wage.
choice: They decided to quit the job because the pay was too low.
outcome: They left the position, the boss at Company D was understanding, and HR warned them about discussing wages.
main_reason: low wage
quote: When I quit the Company C/D job I informed the boss that my wage was the only reason I was leaving.
author: lilydi989898

situation: They needed to resign in Germany before the end of the month to avoid an extra month of notice, but HR was absent from the office.
choice: They arranged a meeting with HR, told them they wanted to leave at the end of the notice period, and sent a scanned resignation for confirmation.
outcome: HR accepted the resignation, sent a confirmation, and the original copy was delivered to HR through a colleague.

advice: Schedule a meeting with HR, send a scanned resignation for written confirmation, and have the original delivered by a colleague.
author: GeologicalWren

situation: they resigned from a small company after a year, citing a desire for a higher position in a different field and a relationship with a coworker
choice: they decided to leave for a higher position in a different field
outcome: they left on good terms with everyone, but now face an awkward invitation to a company event as a significant other
main_reason: they wanted to work in their desired field and advance their career
quote: I left on good terms with everyone.
author: BelethorsGeneralGoods

situation: they were employed at a software firm in India, trained in testing but working on a Java project, and received an offer for a Java developer role elsewhere
choice: they resigned from their current job after receiving the new offer
outcome: their designation was changed to software test analyst in the experience and relieving letters
main_reason: they wanted to join the new company as a Java developer
advice: ensure the new employer is aware of the designation discrepancy and provide supporting documents
quote: My designation was software analyst when I attended interview and it is Software test analyst now.
author: Vishal

situation: They were hired urgently as a technical support engineer for a several‑month project.
choice: They resigned after one week on the job.
